_why: Owner ruling 2026-08-30: `CREATE STREAM x AS SELECT ... INTO y WITH (...)` declares TWO sinks — `x` from CREATE STREAM and `y` from INTO — and is therefore invalid SQL. Named sources and sinks via WITH properties make INTO redundant. The original framing (parse INTO and wire the sink) was WRONG; there is nothing to wire. The defect is that invalid SQL parses successfully and deploys, because the create-path sub-parser stops at INTO and parse_query never checks the input was consumed (#1928).

anchors._note: create path — does NOT handle TokenType::Into, stops there
the other create path — same omission
the ONLY place INTO is handled — plain parse_select, which builds InsertInto. This is the contrast: supported on one path, silently dropped on the other two.

blast_radius._note: Measured across src/ tests/ examples/ at 274a3a7cb. Related: parse_select_no_with 2 files / 5 refs, TokenType::Into 4 files / 4 refs. The parser change is small; the REAL work is the 8 shipped statements in 4 example .sql files that use the two-sink shape and must be rewritten to the named-sink form, each requiring a per-statement decision about which of the two names is the intended sink.

grammar_reference._note: The supported spelling is `CREATE STREAM <sink> AS SELECT ... FROM <source> WITH ('<source>.type'=..., '<sink>.type'=...)`. Named source/sink properties are the mechanism that makes INTO redundant. Do not invent syntax; if a shape is not in these documents, STOP.

tests._note: Each a mutation-kill: break it, confirm failure, restore, confirm pass; log the proof. `plain_select_into_still_parses` is a REGRESSION GUARD — `SELECT ... INTO x` on the plain path is currently supported and is NOT in scope to remove (that is an open owner decision on #1935). Only the CTAS/CSAS position is rejected.

stop_conditions: rewriting a shipped statement requires guessing which of the two names is the intended sink AND the file gives no signal — STOP and report that statement rather than guessing
rejecting INTO on the create path breaks more than 5 existing tests — STOP and report the list
the fix appears to require the #1928 end-of-input check to land first — STOP and report; these are meant to be independently landable
